articles.title: RESEARCH ACCELERATION: THE VIEW INSIDE OPENAI
articles.summary: OpenAI believes that Artificial General Intelligence must be democratically governed for it to benefit all humanity. This can only happen through an informed public debate on the capabilities, risks, and safeguards of highly capable AI systems. The company has released details of its progress towards Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in recent months. It plans to continue to be transparent about its progress with RSI and believes that other companies should be required to publicly track their progress as well.

articles.title: TIM COOK'S CEO-LIKE PAY PACKAGE SHOWS HE ISN'T GOING ANYWHERE
articles.summary: Tim Cook remains a powerful center of gravity at Apple. He will play an especially crucial role in certain areas, such as the company's dealings with the US and China, and its handling of the memory shortage. Cook will get a base salary of $2 million, twice the typical base salary of senior vice presidents and members of the C-suite. He will also receive cash bonuses and stock units that vest over time. The salary clearly shows that Cook's role will be very active.

articles.title: TRAVIS KALANICK'S ATOMS MIGHT BE GETTING INTO THE ROBOTAXI BUSINESS

The company is also in discussions with Uber about how Uber can use Atoms' robotaxi technology. Uber has invested $100 million in Atoms. Kalanick has been cagey about his plans for the startup, but the recent moves could make it a major player in the autonomous vehicle industry.

articles.title: THE CURIOUSLY PLAYABLE UNIVERSE
articles.summary: A domain becomes playable when enough of its complexity can be compressed into a state where there is some reasonably stable repertoire of actions, interactions can be repeated, outcomes provide feedback about better and worse play, and the environment is stationary enough that lessons learned yesterday remain useful tomorrow. None of these conditions need to be perfect, as playability is a matter of degree. Far more of reality than we have previously expected can be turned into a game. Once something can be turned into a game, then it's possible to create a system that can beat it.

articles.title: AN INTERVIEW WITH OPENAI PRESIDENT GREG BROCKMAN ABOUT ASTRA AND ALIGNMENT
articles.summary: OpenAI's president and co-founder, Greg Brockman, dropped out of college in 2010 to join Stripe. He eventually rose to become the company's CTO. He left in 2015 and co-founded OpenAI, where he served as CTO, and after a few years, he is now the company's president. This post features an interview with Brockman recorded before the announcement of Astra. It covers Brockman's background, the ChatGPT launch, OpenAI's place in the value chain, the company's commitment to alignment, the Hugging Face incident, and more.

articles.title: THE LOOP CLOSES
articles.summary: AI models are now capable of taking a request from Slack and then building a feature from end-to-end, with humans just having to click 'merge' or 'deploy' at the end. There's not really much left for humans to do. Humans are still better at absorbing, parsing, and sharing context with each other. However, once that can be automated, the loop will finally be closed, and there will be nothing left to do but to pay the bill.
